newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates steady ahead of liquidity pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates steady ahead of liquidity pact.

text.p: Dutch money rates held largely steady in low-volume trade on Thursday as the holiday season took hold.
Overnight guilders edged up a touch ahead of a new special advances pact due to be announced at 1400 GMT today, quoting at three percent bid from 2.98 percent on Wednesday.
Traders reported little activity in longer-dated money, where prices have trodden water for close on a week now.
A one-basis point increase in the price of August and September Dutch Treasury Certificates to 3.08 percent and 3.10 percent respectively failed to tempt the market.
"I've seen no primary or secondary dealing in DTCs today," one trader said.
The guilder was quoting at 112.60 per 100 marks around 1230 GMT versus 112.571 on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected the new special advances pact to be set at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent.
